label: Final copy step of length-4 sequences (output orig(3))
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.9% of mass) and is a sequence-position detector: on the last copy step of L=4 sequences (t=7, input orig(2), output orig(3)) it fires on essentially every sequence (precision ~1.0) and these are all of its strongest activations (top two quartiles fully covered). Weaker, inconsistent spillover onto the last two copy steps of L=5 sequences (recall_idx 3-4, ~29% / ~12% firing rate, about 15% of mass) and the last copy step of L=3 (~1% of mass); no token-identity, digit-count or repeat condition explains which L=5 sequences fire. Token identity barely modulates it (all in/out tokens lift ~1.1-2.5x). Silent in the original phase, at the delimiter, on early copy steps, and for L>=6.

issues: Every factual claim I checked holds. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0000, recall 0.667, F1 0.800 and mass recall 0.839, and it covers the top two activation quartiles fully (1.0, 1.0). Of 72,934 predicted steps, only 1 is a false positive (e y y y <DEL> e y y).

The profile confirms the location claims. 99.9% of activation mass is in the copy phase, the original phase holds 0.1% and the delimiter 0. The rest splits as: L=4 has 83.8% of mass, L=5 has 15.0%, L=3 has 0.9%, and L>=6 together about 0.4%.

The misses are systematic, not scattered noise, but the explanation already says so. They are L=5 recall_idx 3 (dev precision 0.29) and recall_idx 4 (precision 0.12), and they are weak. L=5 recall_idx 3 accounts for 63% of the lowest activation quartile, 24% of the second and 0% of the top two.

I could not find what decides which L=5 sequences fire. Vowel output, a digit in the last original token, a digit in the first original token, sequences with no digits, and repeated input all left precision around 0.27-0.33, close to the 0.29 base rate. This matches the agent's report that nothing it tried worked.
Widening the predicate to recall_idx==3 & L<=5 raises mass recall to 0.946, but test F1 drops to 0.73 because precision falls to 0.62. The original predicate is the best single rule I found.
Minor caveat: F1 sits exactly on the 0.80 threshold. The label describes the dominant, strongest activations and does not overclaim relative to the predicate.
